messages.subject: Step counter in GGIR
parts:
Hello GGIR User Group,


I am going to start working on a step counter for GGIR and am interested in hearing opinions on what algorithm to implement and what data-set to train and test on.


I propose using this algorithm: Gu et al, 2017 (https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/7885036)


I propose to use this data-set for training / testing - http://cecas.clemson.edu/~ahoover/pedometer/


If anybody has any input on what algorithm / data-set to use I would be more than happy to hear it.


Thanks, Matt

 


Matthew Patterson, PhD

messages.author: 5636dac60e2efbc1
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Step counter in GGIR
parts:
Hi Scott,

I have started on development of an algorithm to count steps from raw acceleration data from the wrist. I am currently using this open source data-set from Clemson as training / testing data - http://cecas.clemson.edu/~ahoover/pedometer/

I would be happy to include your data as part of the training and testing data-sets. To use your data I would require two files for each test 1: raw tri axial wrist acceleration data and 2: sample locations of each step. Is your data already annotated?

Do you have a detailed description of your data collection protocol?

Thanks, talk soon, Matt
